source: NCERT Class XII, Themes in Indian History Part I, Ch. 4 (Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings).

sections.heading: 1. New Religious Ideas (c. 600 BCE)
points: A period of intense debate; new questions about life, sacrifice and the self challenged **Vedic ritualism**.
The **Upanishads** discussed ideas of **atman (self) and Brahman (universal reality)**.
New teachers arose, including **Mahavira (Jainism)** and **Buddha (Buddhism)**.

sections.heading: 2. Jainism and Buddhism
points: **Jainism (Mahavira, 24th Tirthankara)** — stresses **ahimsa (non-violence)**, the **Three Jewels (Triratna): right faith, right knowledge, right conduct**; strict asceticism.

**Buddhism (Gautama Buddha)** — the **Four Noble Truths** (suffering, cause, cessation, path) and the **Eightfold Path (Middle Way)**; concept of **nirvana**; rejected extreme austerity and Vedic ritual.
Buddhist teachings preserved in the **Tripitaka** (Vinaya, Sutta, Abhidhamma Pitakas).

sections.heading: 3. Stupas and Buddhist Art
points: **Stupas** — mounds housing relics of the Buddha; e.g. **Sanchi, Bharhut, Amaravati**.
The **Sanchi Stupa** was preserved partly due to **Shahjehan Begum and Sultan Jehan Begum of Bhopal**; studied/documented by **John Marshall**.
Sculpture depicted the Buddha first through **symbols (aniconic)** and later in **human form (Mathura/Gandhara)**.
**Mahayana** Buddhism (Bodhisattvas, Buddha worship) developed alongside **Hinayana/Theravada**.

sections.heading: 4. Puranic Hinduism and Temples
points: **Puranic Hinduism** — worship of **Vishnu, Shiva, and the Goddess (Devi)**; concept of **avatars (Vishnu's incarnations)** and **bhakti (devotion)**.
Early **temples** were built (garbhagriha housing the deity); rock-cut architecture developed.
The debates among Buddhists, Jainas and Brahmanical traditions shaped Indian religious history.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Upanishads = atman and Brahman; challenged Vedic ritualism.
Jainism (Mahavira): ahimsa + Three Jewels (Triratna); Buddhism: Four Noble Truths + Eightfold Path.
Buddhist canon = Tripitaka; Sanchi Stupa preserved by the Begums of Bhopal (studied by John Marshall).
Mahayana (Bodhisattvas, Buddha images) vs Hinayana/Theravada.
Puranic Hinduism = Vishnu/Shiva/Devi, avatars, bhakti.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Jainism's Three Jewels = right faith, right knowledge, right conduct**; Buddhism's core = Four Noble Truths + Eightfold Path.
The **Sanchi Stupa** was preserved by the **Begums of Bhopal** (documented by **John Marshall**).
**Mahayana** worships the Buddha as a god and reveres Bodhisattvas (unlike early Theravada).
The **Buddhist canon is the Tripitaka** (three baskets).
